newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: South Australia Aborigines, miners reach agreement.
newsitem.headline: South Australia Aborigines, miners reach agreement.

text.p: A blueprint agreement reached between 14 mining companies, including North Ltd, and key Aboriginal groups provided a blueprint for access to explore in and around South Australia's Gawler Craton, North said on Monday.

Under the agreement, Aboriginal heritage clearance work, which identified areas of cultural importance to Aborigines, would be co-ordinated through one decision-making body representing the five Aboriginal groups in the State's far west, the Aboriginal Legal Rights Movement (ALRM) said.

The area involved covers more than 44,000 sq km stretching to the edge of the Nullarbor Plain, about half of which is inside the prospective Gawler Craton where recent aeromagnetic surveys have prompted a flurry of gold exploration.
"This provides certainty for the mining companies who need to be sure that they are consulting with all relevant groups," the ALRM said in a statement.
A spokesman for North said the companies involved included Pasminco Ltd, Equinox Resources NL, Resolute Ltd, Dominion Mining Ltd, Helix Resources NL and Grenfell Resources NL.

The South Australian Chamber of Mines and Energy said the agreement established a blueprint for commercial agreements between miners and Aboriginal groups and complemented legal requirements on mining companies in the state.
"This is an example of us getting on with business in a native title context which is a moving feast," Chamber chief executive Bob Goreing told Reuters.

Under the agreement, a major Aboriginal heritage clearance survey is expected to begin in the next two weeks, with progressive reports provided to the mining companies to accommodate commercial imperatives.
North managing director Campbell Anderson said in a statement his company had the largest single interest in the area, with exploration tenements over 7,500 sq km.
It would begin calcrete sampling and drilling later this year upon the successful negotiation of its agreement and on completion of the Aboriginal heritage clearance survey.
